title: Microbatch evaluation weeknote — compact quant & onboarding
content:
Weeknote (Apr 26 2028) — quick capture of lab activity, experimental results, and next steps.

Context: focused week on microbatch behavior across compact quant variants (kv-cache interaction for 4-bit/5-bit formats), and the first-stage onboarding for the community LlamaS-34B-instruct model into our serving registry. Goal: establish reliable eval signal for regressions introduced by microbatch scaling and compact-kv encodings, and unblock rollout checklist for Dedicated testing.

Highlights:
- Found reproducible latency bump when microbatch >4 and prefix-caching enabled for 4-bit KV (observed on A100-80GB). Mean p95 token latency increased 18–22% vs baseline even though throughput improved. Suspect lock contention in KV prefetch path.
- Eval harness (suite v2.3) showed small but measurable drop in QA exact-match (EM) for quantized LlamaS-34B-4bit on long-context (>2k tokens) prompts: EM delta -1.9 pts vs fp16 baseline; short-context delta is ~-0.3.
- Initial tokenizer mismatch surfaced on onboarding: a custom whitespace-normalization step in model artifacts caused tokenization drift vs our canonical tokenizer; fixed by normalizer drop-in patch.

Experiments run (summary):
- EXP-428: 4-bit KV + microbatch sizes [1,2,4,8] — A100-80GB, same model weights. Metrics captured: tokens/sec, p95 latency, memory headroom. Result: tokens/sec up to 2.9x at batch=8, but p95 latency increased nonlinearly after batch=4.
- EXP-431: 5-bit-compacted KV (new packing) + batch [1,4,8] — significant lower p95 than 4-bit at batch=8 (p95 down ~9%), but quantization quality slightly worse on arithmetic evals (MSE up 0.6%).
- EXP-437: long-context QA evals (prompts 2k–4k tokens) across fp16, 5-bit, 4-bit — measured EM, F1, and hallucination rate (precision to ground-truth). 4-bit shows EM regression concentrated on examples with multi-hop retrieval chains.

Quick metrics snapshot (median across runs):
- fp16 @ batch=1: tokens/s 120, p95 42ms, QA-EM 78.6
- 4-bit @ batch=1: tokens/s 98, p95 45ms, QA-EM 77.9
- 4-bit @ batch=4: tokens/s 260, p95 52ms, QA-EM 77.3
- 5-bit-packed @ batch=8: tokens/s 340, p95 47ms, QA-EM 77.5

Observations / hypotheses:
- Latency regression at larger microbatch sizes for 4-bit appears tied to concurrent KV prefetch locks; when many microbatches touch overlapping KV segments the runtime serializes some accesses. Instrumentation shows spikes in stall time in kv_prefetch.cc.
- 5-bit packed format reduces memory pressure (fewer deserialization steps) which explains lower p95 at high batch, despite slightly worse numeric fidelity. Might be a sweet spot for Dedicated where throughput matters more.
- QA regressions for long-context likely come from aggressive quantization of feed-forward layers interacting with attention positional interpolation on >2048 sequences.

Action items (next 10 working days):
- IA-1: Add scoped timers around KV prefetch lock paths and surface histograms to Console (owner: Ben). Goal: confirm contention hypothesis by May 3.
- IA-2: Run targeted ablation where we disable per-shard locking in a controlled env (owner: Connor) — measure p95 and tail for batch sizes 4/8.
- IA-3: Produce short report comparing 4-bit vs 5-bit-packed tradeoffs for Dedicated customers (owner: Aisha) — include cost/per-token estimates and SLO guidance. Due: May 10.
- IA-4: Finish tokenizer normalizer patch and add golden tokenization tests for every onboarding model (owner: Marta). Blockers: need integration test infra update (CI job increase).
- IA-5: Add specific long-context evaluation slices to eval harness: multi-hop, retrieval-chain, code-generation with >3k tokens (owner: Samir).

Blockers / risks:
- CI resource quota currently prevents running full horizon long-context sweeps in parallel; we need temporary quota bump from infra to complete full matrix by EOW.
- Dedicated SLA customers may prefer throughput over small EM regressions; we need UX guidance on when to prefer 5-bit-packed vs 4-bit for rollout.

Notes from standup sync (Apr 25):
- Infra said they can spin up two extra A100 nodes for 48h window — Connor to coordinate.
- Solutions eng asked for a short playbook paragraph on choosing batch size vs latency; draft in PR #842 (linked).
- Customer success flagged a Dedicated trial where observed slowdown at peak traffic; proposed quick fallback to fp16 on critical routes.

Decisions and tradeoffs logged:
- For now, default onboarding config will use 5-bit-packed for Dedicated experiments where expected throughput > 1.5x baseline. 4-bit remains default for hosted experiments with strict quality gates. Documented in onboarding checklist (CON-5642).

Open questions for next week:
- Can we design a hybrid KV layout that keeps deserialization cheap but preserves 4-bit numeric fidelity?
- If lock contention is confirmed, should we implement striping by request-id vs shard-id? Impact analysis required.
- What are budgeted infra hours to rerun full eval matrix for top 5 customer models?

Useful links / references:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/842 (microbatch prefetch timers)
- Jira: AI-1987 (quant-variant-eval-matrix), CON-5642 (onboarding-checklist)
